newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sells record 288 trln lira of t-bills.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sells record 288 trln lira of t-bills.

text.p: The Turkish Treasury sold a record high 288.2 trillion lira of 238-day t-bills in an auction on Tuesday at slightly lower yields.
The central bank said bids totalled a record 480.6 trillion for the papers with June 4, 1997 maturity, the longest issued so far this year.
The average and maximum yields eased to 130 72 and 131.31 percent from 131.20 and 131.74 percent, respectively in the previous 217-day t-bill auction on October 1.

Paper demand at t-bill auctions has been on the rise in the past three weeks after the government announced plans to introduce a 10 percent witholding tax on interest income from t-bills and bonds from 1997.
Bankers said strong demand was seen because the Treasury has said the new tax would not be retroactive after it takes effect with a related cabinet decree to be published.
Banks will on Wednesday pay 164 trillion lira to the Treasury for the auction, to be offset by 145.2 trillion lira of t-bill maturities.
The Treasury gradually extended the maturity of the bills it auctioned to June 1997 from March in the last three weekly auctions. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
